item.title: Solved: How to Install Node.js Dependencies on Windows with Python
item.description:
I recently delved into a Node.js codebase requiring the installation of dependencies via NPM, particularly jQuery. However, I encountered persistent issues while executing the command:

npm install jquery

Upon running this command, the console returned a daunting series of error messages indicating that the system could not find the Python executable required for the installation of certain packages. Here is a snippet of the output:

gyp ERR! stack Error: Can't find Python executable "python", you can set the PYTHON env variable.

This message suggests a misconfiguration of Python on my system, which is a crucial component when using NPM to install packages that compile native modules. The detailed error log highlights multiple HTTP requests for dependencies and ultimately fails at the node-gyp rebuild step. This issue commonly arises in environments where Python 2.x is mandated, as many Node.js modules depend on it for building.
